proves.facet: The production Node listing script with a controlled daemon leaves both unreached recorded IDs unknown on a cursorless incomplete census; a completed census returns the live manager and known-empty archived orchestrator.

1.note: The scoped current source carries the module/document behavior described above.

2.note: The real Node bridge script also runs against a scripted daemon client that enforces 200-entry listing pages. Cases pin complete pagination, archived-ID filtering, the ten-page bound and `hasMore` without a next cursor. A tree-reader composition proves missing IDs from an incomplete census stay `agents: null`, while a completed listing resolves the recorded live/archived agents. This is native-script/controlled-client evidence, not installed-host consumption.

3.note:
The same complete/incomplete census is applied to the document tree and developer seat list.
